Description: Implementation-level logging field for the time spent loading and preparing a training batch before model computation.
How and when it is used: Recorded during training to monitor data pipeline efficiency and identify I/O bottlenecks.
Range of values and meaning: Measured in seconds; lower values indicate faster data preparation.
Known limitations: Reflects system efficiency rather than model quality. Can vary with storage speed and preprocessing load.

Description: OpenFold implements distogram loss by binning pseudo-beta pair distances and applying softmax cross-entropy to the predicted distogram logits.
How and when it is used: Used during each training step as one component of the total loss to supervise pairwise spatial relationships.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Does not directly represent final 3D structure quality on its own.

Description: Auxiliary loss for the experimentally resolved head, which predicts whether atom-level positions are resolved in the experimental structure; in OpenFold config this head has c_out = 37, consistent with the atom37 representation.
How and when it is used: Used during training as an auxiliary supervision signal.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Less intuitive than geometric metrics and contributes indirectly to structural quality.

Description: OpenFold computes FAPE with compute_fape(...), comparing predicted and target positions in local rigid frames, with normalization and optional clamping.
How and when it is used: One of the main structure-learning losses during training.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Harder to interpret directly than RMSD or lDDT for non-experts.

Description: Confidence-head training loss associated with local confidence prediction; conceptually linked to pLDDT but implemented as a loss term in AlphaFold/OpenFold training rather than the final pLDDT score itself.
How and when it is used: Used during training to help the model learn confidence estimation.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: This is a training loss, not the predicted pLDDT score itself.

Description: Auxiliary self-supervised loss for predicting masked tokens in the MSA representation.
How and when it is used: Used during training to improve evolutionary representation learning from MSAs.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: More related to internal representation learning than direct structure accuracy.

Description: OpenFold explicitly defines this as implementing Algorithm 27 (torsionAngleLoss) for supervising side-chain torsion angles and angle normalization.
How and when it is used: Used during training to improve side-chain geometry.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Good side-chain loss does not necessarily imply correct global folding.

Description: Geometry-based penalty for structural violations such as bond or angle inconsistencies and clashes, following AlphaFold-style structural-violation terms.
How and when it is used: Used during training to encourage chemically and geometrically valid predictions.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Can be numerically large and should be interpreted together with the total loss.

Description: Implementation-level aggregate recorded in loss_breakdown, representing the raw combined objective magnitude before the final logged total loss is reported.
How and when it is used: Used for internal monitoring of the raw magnitude of training objectives.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Not always directly comparable across different configurations or implementations.

Description: Final aggregate loss returned by self.loss(...) and logged from the loss_breakdown or training step output.
How and when it is used: Main optimization target during each training step.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Aggregates multiple objectives, so improvements do not indicate which subcomponent changed.

Description: Implementation-level progress field indicating the current training epoch written through the training logger.
How and when it is used: Used to track training progress at a coarse level.
Range of values and meaning: Integer starting from 0; larger values indicate later training stages.
Known limitations: Epoch counts are not always directly comparable across datasets of different sizes.

Description: Implementation-level progress field indicating the current optimization step.
How and when it is used: Used to track fine-grained training progress.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative integer; larger values indicate more updates have been performed.
Known limitations: Step count depends on batch size and logging frequency.

Description: Implementation-level progress field indicating the cumulative number of optimization updates across epochs.
How and when it is used: Used in epoch summary logs to reference model progress precisely.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative integer; larger values indicate later training progress.
Known limitations: Like step count, it depends on batch configuration and logging schedule.

Description: Implementation-level logging field for the time spent on forward and backward computation and parameter update for a training step.
How and when it is used: Used during training to monitor computational efficiency.
Range of values and meaning: Measured in seconds; lower values indicate faster computation.
Known limitations: Depends heavily on hardware, sequence length, and batch properties.

Description: Mean distogram loss across all training steps within one epoch.
How and when it is used: Used in epoch-level summaries to track the average trend of distogram supervision.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Averages may hide high variance within the epoch.

Description: Mean experimentally-resolved loss over one epoch.
How and when it is used: Used in epoch summaries to assess the average auxiliary supervision trend.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: More indirect than geometric quality metrics.

Description: Mean FAPE across all training steps within one epoch.
How and when it is used: Used to monitor epoch-level changes in geometric learning quality.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Averaging may conceal step-level instabilities.

Description: Mean pLDDT-related confidence loss over one epoch.
How and when it is used: Used to summarize confidence-prediction learning across an epoch.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Does not equal the actual predicted pLDDT score.

Description: Mean masked MSA loss over one epoch.
How and when it is used: Used to summarize sequence-evolution learning over an epoch.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Less directly tied to 3D structure quality.

Description: Mean supervised chi-angle loss over one epoch.
How and when it is used: Used to summarize side-chain learning quality across an epoch.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Does not by itself guarantee correct global structure.

Description: Mean structural violation penalty over one epoch.
How and when it is used: Used to summarize geometric validity across the epoch.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Can dominate numerically and should be interpreted together with other metrics.

Description: Mean raw combined loss over one epoch before final scaling.
How and when it is used: Used to track average raw objective magnitude at epoch level.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Limited interpretability without knowing the weighting scheme.

Description: Mean total training loss over one epoch.
How and when it is used: Main epoch-level convergence metric.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Does not indicate which specific component is improving or worsening.

Measure name: Local Distance Difference Test on Cα
Description: In OpenFold training, lddt_ca is computed by calling lddt_ca(...) on predicted and ground-truth coordinates with per_residue=False, then stored as metrics['lddt_ca'].
How and when it is used: Used in epoch summaries to evaluate how well the predicted structure matches the ground truth.
Range of values and meaning: Usually between 0 and 1; higher is better. Values closer to 1 indicate better local structural agreement.
Known limitations: Focuses on local geometry and may not fully reflect global topology correctness.

Description: In OpenFold training, drmsd_ca is computed by applying drmsd(...) to masked Cα coordinates from prediction and ground truth; it is an implementation-specific Cα distance error metric, not exactly the same as standard superposition-based RMSD.
How and when it is used: Used in epoch summaries as a structural error metric.
Range of values and meaning: Non-negative real value; lower is better.
Known limitations: Not identical to standard RMSD; sensitive to structural scale and implementation details.
